So, you visited three buildings this week. Which one is the best?
Building A is beautiful, but it's too far from the hospital. It takes forty minutes by car.
That's too long for the families. What about Building B?
It's very close, but it's too noisy. There's too much traffic on that street.
OK. And the last one, Building C?
Building C is my favorite. The apartments are bright, and the rent is affordable.
Great. Is there an elevator? A lot of our patients can't use the stairs.
Yes, there is. The only downside is the kitchen. It isn't big enough for two families.
That's OK. Do you have enough money for six apartments there?
Not for six. We have enough money for four. The landlord is very flexible, so maybe more next year.

Good morning, Mr. Varela. This is Carlos Andrade, the landlord of Building C. Thank you for your visit on Tuesday. I have good news for you. I have four apartments for you from January, and for a hospital project, I can lower the rent a little: two thousand five hundred reais a month. I know the kitchens aren't big enough for two families, so I can take out one wall in two of the apartments. The elevator is new, and the street is quiet, not noisy at all. And one more thing: there is a supermarket and a pharmacy on the same street, so it's very convenient for the families. Please call me back this week. Thank you.

Hi Fernando, it's Ana, from the housing pilot. I talked to the families about Building C, and they like it a lot. But they have two worries. First, the bus stop near the building is very crowded in the morning, and some patients are too tired to stand for a long time. Maybe we can use the hospital van. Second, the bedrooms are bright, but in the afternoon they are too hot. We need fans, or maybe air conditioning. And one good thing: the families say the street is quiet enough for the children to sleep. So I think it's a good choice. Let's talk tomorrow. Bye!
